Digital media store |accessableby=Android devices, {{wp|Chrome OS}}, Web |externallink=[https://play.google.com/ play.google.com] }} '''Google Play''' (formerly '''Android Market''') is a digital distribution service owned and operated by {{wp|Google}} and is the official app store for the {{wp|Android}} operating system. Along with Android apps, the service also sells movies, TV shows and books. The service is linked to Google's online video-sharing platform [[YouTube]]; movies and TV shows purchased on Google Play are watchable on YouTube. ==Games & apps== The Android Market launched on October 22, 2008 and rebranded as Google Play on March 6, 2012[https://googleblog.blogspot.com/2012/03/introducing-google-play-all-your.html ''Introducing Google Play: All your entertainment, anywhere you go'' - Official Google Blog] (retrieved April 28, 2020). It is the official app store of Android, and as of March 2020, it had 2,870,000 apps available for download[https://www.statista.com/statistics/266210/number-of-available-applications-in-the-google-play-store/ ''Number of available applications in the Google Play Store'' - Statista] (retrieved April 28, 2020). ===Available Pokémon games & apps=== {{main|:Category:Mobile games|List of mobile games}} ==Movies & TV== Google TV launched in May 2011 as Google Movies[https://mashable.com/2011/05/10/google-movies-android/ ''Google Launches Movies for Android'' - Mashable] (retrieved April 28, 2020), and rebranded with the rest of Google Play in March 2012 as Google Play Movies (later becoming Google Play Movies & TV and then Google TV in September 2020).[https://www.theverge.com/2020/9/30/21492549/google-tv-app-play-movies-name-change-chromecast Google Play Movies & TV is now Google TV but it’s not the same Google TV that runs on Android TV on the new Chromecast, it’s an app - The Verge] It is possible to purchase or rent movies in over 110 countries, and TV shows are available to purchase in {{pmin|Australia}}, Austria, {{pmin|Canada}}, {{pmin|France}}, {{pmin|Germany}}, Japan, Switzerland, the {{pmin|the United Kingdom|United Kingdom}}, and the {{pmin|the United States|United States}}[https://support.google.com/googleplay/answer/2843119 ''Country availability for Google Play apps & digital content'' - Google Play Help] (retrieved April 28, 2020). Purchases and rentals are viewable via the Google Play Movies & TV app, the Google Play website, the YouTube app or the YouTube website. ===Available Pokémon anime=== {{main|List of digital home video releases of Pokémon animation}} ===Available Pokémon movies=== {{main|List of digital home video releases of Pokémon animation#Movies|List of digital home video releases of Pokémon animation → Movies}} ==Music== Google Music launched publicly on November 16, 2011, after a six-month closed beta[https://www.theverge.com/2011/11/16/2566928/google-music-store-announcement ''Google Music store official: artist hubs, Google+ integration, and more'' - The Verge] (retrieved April 28, 2020), and rebranded to Google Play Music in March 2012. The service offered music for sale, as well as a subscription service that allowed for unlimited listening to its music library for a monthly fee. After the relaunch of [[YouTube#YouTube Music|YouTube Music]] in 2019, Google confirmed that Google Play Music was to be replaced with the new service[https://www.digitaltrends.com/music/what-happens-to-google-play-music-youtube-music/ ''YouTube Music is replacing Google Play Music: Here’s where, when, and why'' - Digital Trends] (retrieved April 28, 2020), and between September and October of 2020 the Google Play Music service and store permanently shut down[https://techcrunch.com/2020/08/05/google-play-music-to-shut-down-starting-in-september-will-disappear-by-december/ ''Google Play Music to shut down starting in September, will disappear by December'' - TechCrunch] (retrieved October 1, 2020).
